releases.name: SpecTorque 0.2.0 · pilot prerelease
releases.body:
This build adds an EN/ES pilot walkthrough, an installed Codex Desktop viewer, and reviewed refinement and export paths across the local workbench and native integrations. Use the standalone workbench for the pilot. After installation, it analyzes, reviews and exports local files without a model, account or GPU.

- Follow the [release installation guide](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/blob/v0.2.0/docs/releases.md). Verify the downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.
- Replay the original synthetic examples in English or Spanish from the demo ZIP. Findings cite exact source lines, and unknowns remain visible.
- The Codex Desktop viewer was exercised on macOS arm64 with an existing profile and a bounded host model turn. The final workbench fix was exercised in Desktop in English, with Spanish browser coverage and an intermediate Desktop pass. See the [qualification record](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/blob/v0.2.0/docs/codex-desktop-probe.md#020-candidate-qualification-on-macos-arm64). Windows Desktop, a clean Desktop profile and VoiceOver remain unqualified. The shared VS Code route remains a preview.
- The [participant pilot](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/issues/8) remains open. The demo and technical checks use synthetic fixtures. No participant outcomes are reported here.

Built from `fb6e72f5519e8434f9c0b9c9d6b357e4ed1192f0`. Two independent builds with Node 22.20.0 produced identical installer archives. The demo manifest records the source commit and installer digests. See the [promotion checks and installed host qualification](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/pull/42/checks).

releases.name: SpecTorque 0.1.0 · executable preview
releases.body:
Initial executable preview of SpecTorque, released under Apache-2.0 with separately attributed EPIC-derived material. This is not the completed December V1.

Create editable spec/plan/task artifacts, import Markdown or a bounded workspace/public GitHub revision, inspect forty EPIC heuristic checks with exact source evidence, review refinements, track pending decisions and export revision-bound reports plus feature-scoped Markdown ZIP archives. Basic operation needs no model, GPU or credentials.

Includes CLI, six read-only MCP tools, three portable skills, a React workbench, a Claude Code Mod, a VS Code extension for use alongside Codex, an OpenCode TUI adapter and a Pi extension. The compatibility matrix distinguishes real-client smoke tests, native harness checks and remaining full acceptance.

Validation: 27 tests, TypeScript and production build; The release commit passed Node 22 CI on Ubuntu and Windows and all 27 tests locally on macOS with Node 22.20.0. Its hosted macOS job was queued at publication; the earlier preview revision had passed all three hosted platforms. Installed tarball and standalone bundled CLI exercised. Claude manifest/native render harness passed; real Claude pane opens; OpenCode and Pi performed reviewed scratch-file edits without model inference. The VSIX is packaged; its full real-client walkthrough remains open.

Installation and tested versions: [release guide](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/blob/v0.1.0/docs/releases.md), [compatibility](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/blob/v0.1.0/docs/compatibility.md). Delivery targets remain December 1 (operational), December 4 (native views), December 11 (stabilized). Work tracking: [milestones](https://github.com/jayanez/spec-torque/milestones).

Use SHA256SUMS to verify the five downloadable packages. Heuristic scores do not certify specification correctness or predict defect reduction.
